source.title: Yuan 1.0: Large-Scale Pre-trained Language Model in Zero-Shot and Few-Shot Learning
source.authors: Shaohua Wu; Xudong Zhao; Tong Yu; Rong-Guo Zhang; Chong Shen; Hongli Liu; Feng Li; Hong Zhu; Jiangang Luo; Liang Xu; Xuanwei Zhang

page_placements.theme: Within-run and narrow-range loss observations have limited scaling implications

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and discusses scaling as motivation, but does not test the stated scaling laws. Its own loss results are training loss for one Yuan run, not held-out-loss scaling or compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports Yuan 245B training-loss values and a described training-loss curve, but does not measure held-out loss across model sizes, token counts, or compute budgets, fit power laws, test extrapolation, or assess compute-optimal allocations. GPT-3 and PanGu-α entries in Table 9 are comparison values, not results newly tested here, so they are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: Yuan 1.0 is a model-building paper. It cites Kaplan et al. as motivation but reports no held-out loss across sizes, tokens or compute, fits no power law, and tests no extrapolation, allocation, shape effect or downstream predictability. Its only loss results are training loss for one 245B run (Table 9, Fig. 6).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that Yuan 1.0 (245B, trained on a 5TB Chinese corpus) achieves SOTA on ZeroCLUE, FewCLUE and generation tasks. They also conclude that calibration and label expansion steadily improve zero- and few-shot accuracy, and that LM beats PLM in zero-shot while PLM is better with fine-tuning. They draw no conclusion about scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains and evaluates Yuan models; it does not reproduce the scaling-law measurement method.

fits_no_version.finding: Yuan 245B reaches a training loss of 1.64 after 180B tokens. Its training curve falls rapidly over the first 10B tokens, then flattens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single large run's training loss falls fast early and then flattens. This says nothing about held-out-loss scaling across runs.

record.problems: The loss evidence relevant to scaling is limited to a single Yuan 245B training run; the curve is described qualitatively, and no held-out losses, fitted laws, uncertainty estimates, or controls are reported. The comparison values for other models are not newly tested in this paper.
record.rows_left_out: GPT-3 and PanGu-α values in Table 9 are comparison values rather than results newly tested by this study; excluded under the rule against extracting cited results.

untested.parts: No held-out loss measured across parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-run fits used to predict larger runs.
No fixed-compute comparison of how to split parameters and tokens.
No loss comparison across depth or width at fixed parameters. Layer and hidden-size choices were made for parallel-training throughput, not for loss.
No other modalities or training regimes tested for a power law.
Downstream scores are reported for 13B and 245B models. These have different token counts and evaluation setups, and the paper makes no scale-trend or loss-predictability analysis.
No fitted exponents and no fitting-choice analysis.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/cites_only call is correct. Table 9's GPT-3 and PanGu-α training losses are cited comparison values, not new results. They were correctly left out as rows. The losses are also on different corpora, so they could not support a scaling comparison anyway.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining-loss scaling sweep across parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits or predictions of larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation comparison or parameter/token scaling with compute.
No comparison of held-out loss across architectures at fixed parameter count.
No power-law test in other modalities or training regimes.
Downstream task scores are reported, but not as a predictability test against scale or pretraining loss.
No fitted exponents, setup-sensitivity analysis, or test for departures from a single power law.
